data.body:
IMPLEMENTED AND MERGED — Gerrit change 1696, merged as 61b49deaa6 (Verified +1, LLM-Review +1).

MECHANISM CONFIRMED, THEN CLOSED. `_prepare_event` created the ticket directory with
`os.makedirs` OUTSIDE the write lock and landed its first event only at the under-lock
`os.replace`. New leaf module `src/rebar/_store/staging.py` (267 LOC) builds the directory
and its first event together in a staging path and publishes them with ONE `os.rename`.
The rename still happens UNDER the write lock, so an event is never visible before the
rebase guard and `under_lock_check` have passed (AC3: lock discipline unchanged).

TEMP-PATH CONVENTION CHOSEN: `<tracker>/.tmp-newticket-<pid>-<uuid4hex>`.
The leading dot is deliberately NOT a new rule — `fsck._ticket_dirs`,
`fsck.foreign_store_path_list`, fsck's JSON check and `relation_snapshot` ALREADY skip
dot-prefixed top-level entries, and ticket ids never start with a dot, so temp paths are
invisible to both checks with ZERO scanner change. Same convention `.tmp-event-*` relies
on. pid+uuid4 make each staging name unique per writer and per call (AC3).

AC2 — RED PROVEN BEFORE GREEN. Against unmodified origin/main the injection reproduced the
exact production signature:
    MISSING_CREATE: 0efe-9207-2706-43a3 — no CREATE event found
    FOREIGN_STORE_PATH: ... 1 top-level path ... working-tree strays
i.e. the illsuited-erect-ibis signature, on one of the very ids swept there. Re-running the
committed test file against the old writer fails 3 tests and passes 6; with the fix all 9
pass. The interruption is injected at the write lock — a genuine failure mode inside the
vulnerable window, and shape-independent, so RED and GREEN are compared honestly rather
than by patching a symbol only one shape calls.

AC4 — AUDIT RESULT. Converted: `batch_stage_and_commit` (it SHARES `_prepare_event`, so it
carried the identical window — this was missed in my first plan and caught by the
plan-review gate), `inbound_translate._write_event_file` (its mkdir preceded
`finalize_event`, which can refuse an event outright via the secret screen), and the
`dispatch_one` BRIDGE_ALERT emission (an error path, where interruption is most likely).
`_rollback_batch` now also removes a directory the batch itself published once its event is
gone — otherwise a failed create re-created the very debris this closes.
Exempt with reasons: `lock.py::_acquire_mkdir` (dot-prefixed `.ticket-write.lock.d`,
invisible to fsck, and its mkdir->stamp gap already has a staleness adjudicator);
`hlc.py` and `fsck_repair.py` marker dirs (under `.rebar/` or the resolved git dir, outside
the committed worktree); `session_log.py` / `identity.py` / `trusted_env_cmd.py` pointer and
config writers (not in the tracker at all).

043f BOUNDARY RESPECTED. The sweep reclaims only `.tmp-newticket-*` — the writer's own
staging area — and only when the owner is provably gone, reusing the write lock's v2
host + pid-namespace + process-start-time stamp so pid recycling cannot fool it. It never
touches a ticket directory; a test pins that an event-less ticket directory SURVIVES the
sweep. 043f's ruling (a reader tolerates, never tidies, and thereby also repairs clones
already carrying debris) is untouched — only the writer-side "dir before first event"
decision is superseded. Said so in the code comment, in the module docstring, and in
docs/concurrency.md.

AC5 — make lint and make typecheck clean; 466 store tests, 3067 reconciler/bridge/
concurrency tests, and the 9 new tests all pass; CI Verified +1 on the merged patchset. No
event-format or committed-layout change (byte parity preserved: the same `canonical_bytes`
/ `canonical_str` output, routed through the shared helper).

NOTE FOR FUTURE READERS: the brief for this ticket said lock.py was at 798/800 LOC. That
was stale — it is 513. The real module-size pressure was `event_append.py` at 796/800, which
is why the logic went into a new module; it now sits at 794 and staging.py at 267.
